queries.colour_code_human_factors: What does human factors research say about designing colour codes for industrial and laboratory labelling? Specifically: how many colours people can reliably identify by absolute judgement, the prevalence and effect of colour vision deficiency (which colour pairs fail for protan, deutan and tritan observers), the benefit of redundant coding (shape, text, position, pattern), the effect of lighting and fading, colour coding for visual search versus identification, and conflicts between an organisational colour code and safety colour standards (ISO 3864, ANSI Z535) or pipe marking (ASME A13.1). Give quantitative findings and cite specific studies (for example Christ 1975, Wickens) and standards.
queries.visual_management_labs: What evidence exists on visual management and 5S practices (floor marking, shadow boards, colour-coded zones, status labels, andon or stack lights) for organisation, cleanliness and safety in research laboratories, cleanrooms and factories, including floors shared with autonomous mobile robots or AGVs (zone and hazard marking under ISO 3691-4 or ANSI/RIA R15.08)? Report measured outcomes (time to find items, errors, accidents, audit scores, cleanliness), and the floor-marking and indicator-light colour conventions in use (for example OSHA 1910.144, IEC 60204-1). Cite specific studies and standards.
queries.colour_machine_vision_labware: Have self-driving laboratories, laboratory automation or industrial robot cells used colour coding (colour-coded caps, labware, tool handles, bins or markers) as a machine-vision check by the robot, alongside or instead of barcodes, QR codes, fiducial markers (AprilTag, ArUco) or RFID? How reliable was colour recognition under changing lighting compared with barcodes or fiducials, and what error-proofing (poka-yoke) results are reported? Cite specific systems and papers.
